summary: Adds a Flask search endpoint and a hardcoded Stripe key, and changes the pagination offset. It also downgrades lodash and loosens the Dockerfile, deploy script and CI workflow.

findings.title: Search query built from request input
findings.description: The search_items handler puts the q request parameter into the SQL text with an f-string. Nothing escapes or binds the value. Any caller of the search endpoint can inject SQL and read or alter the items database. Pass q to cur.execute as a bound parameter with a placeholder.
findings.suggested_change: cur.execute("SELECT id, name, price FROM items WHERE name = ?", (q,))
findings.problem: The search_items handler puts the q request parameter into the SQL text with an f-string. Nothing escapes or binds the value.
findings.consequence: Any caller of the search endpoint can inject SQL and read or alter the items database.
findings.fix: Pass q to cur.execute as a bound parameter with a placeholder.

findings.title: Stripe API key committed to source
findings.description: The config module hardcodes a Stripe API key as a string literal. The key now lives in the git history. Anyone with repository access can use the key to make payment API calls for the shop. Rotate the key and load it from an environment variable or secret store.
findings.problem: The config module hardcodes a Stripe API key as a string literal. The key now lives in the git history.
findings.consequence: Anyone with repository access can use the key to make payment API calls for the shop.
findings.fix: Rotate the key and load it from an environment variable or secret store.

findings.title: Pagination offset skips the first page
findings.description: The list_items handler now computes the offset as page times PAGE_SIZE. Page 1 therefore starts at row 20. Clients never see the first 20 items, and every page shows the next page's rows. Restore the offset as page minus one times PAGE_SIZE.
findings.problem: The list_items handler now computes the offset as page times PAGE_SIZE. Page 1 therefore starts at row 20.
findings.consequence: Clients never see the first 20 items, and every page shows the next page's rows.
findings.fix: Restore the offset as page minus one times PAGE_SIZE.

findings.title: Lodash downgraded to a vulnerable release
findings.description: The change pins lodash from 4.18.1 back to 4.17.15. That release has known command injection and prototype pollution flaws. Front-end code that uses template or path helpers becomes exploitable again. Keep lodash at 4.18.1 or later in package.json and package-lock.json.
findings.problem: The change pins lodash from 4.18.1 back to 4.17.15. That release has known command injection and prototype pollution flaws.
findings.consequence: Front-end code that uses template or path helpers becomes exploitable again.
findings.fix: Keep lodash at 4.18.1 or later in package.json and package-lock.json.

findings.title: Container now runs as root
findings.description: The change removed the useradd step and the USER 10001 line that followed the app copy. The Flask server now runs as root. A compromise of the web app gives the attacker root inside the container. Restore the unprivileged app user and the USER directive before EXPOSE.
findings.problem: The change removed the useradd step and the USER 10001 line that followed the app copy. The Flask server now runs as root.
findings.consequence: A compromise of the web app gives the attacker root inside the container.
findings.fix: Restore the unprivileged app user and the USER directive before EXPOSE.

findings.title: Unguarded recursive delete of deploy directory
findings.description: The change removed the guard against an empty DEPLOY_DIR and dropped the quotes. An empty DEPLOY_DIR makes the command rm -rf /. A deploy run with DEPLOY_DIR set to an empty string wipes the host filesystem. A path with spaces deletes the wrong directories. Restore the quoted form with the empty-value guard.
findings.problem: The change removed the guard against an empty DEPLOY_DIR and dropped the quotes. An empty DEPLOY_DIR makes the command rm -rf /.
findings.consequence: A deploy run with DEPLOY_DIR set to an empty string wipes the host filesystem. A path with spaces deletes the wrong directories.
findings.fix: Restore the quoted form with the empty-value guard.

findings.title: Deploy loop parses ls output
findings.description: The loop now splits unquoted ls output into words. File names with spaces break into pieces, and the loop prints bare names instead of paths. The deploy log shows wrong entries for some files. Restore the glob loop over the quoted directory.
findings.problem: The loop now splits unquoted ls output into words. File names with spaces break into pieces, and the loop prints bare names instead of paths.
findings.consequence: The deploy log shows wrong entries for some files.
findings.fix: Restore the glob loop over the quoted directory.

findings.title: Pull request title expanded inside shell script
findings.description: The workflow puts the pull request title straight into the run script. A title containing quotes or subshells runs as shell code. A pull request author can run arbitrary commands in the CI runner through the title. Pass the title through an env variable and quote that variable in the script.
findings.problem: The workflow puts the pull request title straight into the run script. A title containing quotes or subshells runs as shell code.
findings.consequence: A pull request author can run arbitrary commands in the CI runner through the title.
findings.fix: Pass the title through an env variable and quote that variable in the script.

findings.title: Base image no longer pinned
findings.description: The change replaced the pinned python 3.12.7 slim image with python:latest. Builds now pick up whatever Python release is newest. A new Python major release can break the app build without any code change. Pin the base image to a specific release tag again.
findings.problem: The change replaced the pinned python 3.12.7 slim image with python:latest. Builds now pick up whatever Python release is newest.
findings.consequence: A new Python major release can break the app build without any code change.
findings.fix: Pin the base image to a specific release tag again.

findings.title: Changed endpoints have no covering test
findings.description: The repository has no tests for the new search endpoint or the changed pagination offset. Regressions like the offset error reach users without any check failing. Add tests for search_items and for the first page of list_items.
findings.problem: The repository has no tests for the new search endpoint or the changed pagination offset.
findings.consequence: Regressions like the offset error reach users without any check failing.
findings.fix: Add tests for search_items and for the first page of list_items.
